decim.description:
Factor by which to subsample the data.

Warning

Low-pass filtering is not performed, this simply selects every Nth sample (where N is the value passed to decim), i.e., it compresses the signal (see Notes). If the data are not properly filtered, aliasing artifacts may occur. See :ref:`resampling-and-decimating` for more information.

offset.description: Apply an offset to where the decimation starts relative to the sample corresponding to t=0. The offset is in samples at the current sampling rate.

tshift.description: The (absolute or relative) time shift in seconds. If relative is True, positive tshift increases the time value associated with each sample, while negative tshift decreases it.

relative.description: If True, increase or decrease time values by tshift seconds. Otherwise, shift the time values such that the time of the first sample equals tshift.

If not None, then pandas-style queries may be used to select subsets of data, see :meth:`mne.Epochs.__getitem__`. When the EpochsTFR object is subsetted, the metadata is subsetted accordingly, and the row indices will be modified to match EpochsTFR.selection.

    Extrapolate to four points placed to form a square encompassing all data points, where each side of the square is three times the range of the data in the respective dimension.

  • 'local' (default for MEG sensors)

    Extrapolate only to nearby points (approximately to points closer than median inter-electrode distance). This will also set the mask to be polygonal based on the convex hull of the sensors.

  • 'head' (default for non-MEG sensors)

    Extrapolate out to the edges of the clipping circle. This will be on the head circle when the sensors are contained within the head circle, but it can extend beyond the head when sensors are plotted outside the head circle.

CrossSpectralDensity.description:
Given a list of time series, the CSD matrix denotes for each pair of time series, the cross-spectral density. This matrix is symmetric and internally stored as a vector.

This object can store multiple CSD matrices: one for each frequency. Use .get_data(freq) to obtain an CSD matrix as an ndarray.

fmax.description: Upper bound of the frequency range in Hertz. Defaults to the highest frequency available. When a list of frequencies is given, these are used as the upper bounds (inclusive) of frequency bins and the sum is taken for each bin.

bands.description:
The frequencies or frequency ranges to plot. If a :class:`dict`, keys will be used as subplot titles and values should be either a single frequency (e.g., {'presentation rate': 6.5}) or a length-two sequence of lower and upper frequency band edges (e.g., {'theta': (4, 8)}). If a single frequency is provided, the plot will show the frequency bin that is closest to the requested value. If None (the default), expands to:

bands = {'Delta (0-4 Hz)': (0, 4), 'Theta (4-8 Hz)': (4, 8),
         'Alpha (8-12 Hz)': (8, 12), 'Beta (12-30 Hz)': (12, 30),
         'Gamma (30-45 Hz)': (30, 45)}

Note

For backwards compatibility, :class:`tuples<tuple>` of length 2 or 3 are also accepted, where the last element of the tuple is the subplot title and the other entries are frequency values (a single value or band edges). New code should use :class:`dict` or None.

normalize.description: If True, each band will be divided by the total power. Defaults to False.

dict(marker='o', markerfacecolor='w', markeredgecolor='k',
        linewidth=0, markersize=4)

contours.description: The number of contour lines to draw. If 0, no contours will be drawn. If a positive integer, that number of contour levels are chosen using the matplotlib tick locator (may sometimes be inaccurate, use array for accuracy). If array-like, the array values are used as the contour levels. The values should be in µV for EEG, fT for magnetometers and fT/m for gradiometers. If colorbar=True, the colorbar will have ticks corresponding to the contour levels. Default is 6.

outlines.description: The outlines to be drawn. If 'head', the default head scheme will be drawn. If dict, each key refers to a tuple of x and y positions, the values in 'mask_pos' will serve as image mask. Alternatively, a matplotlib patch object can be passed for advanced masking options, either directly or as a function that returns patches (required for multi-axis plots). If None, nothing will be drawn. Defaults to 'head'.

image_interp.description: The image interpolation to be used. Options are 'cubic' (default) to use :class:`scipy.interpolate.CloughTocher2DInterpolator`, 'nearest' to use :class:`scipy.spatial.Voronoi` or 'linear' to use :class:`scipy.interpolate.LinearNDInterpolator`.

extrapolate.description:
Options:

  • 'box'

    Extrapolate to four points placed to form a square encompassing all data points, where each side of the square is three times the range of the data in the respective dimension.

  • 'local' (default for MEG sensors)

    Extrapolate only to nearby points (approximately to points closer than median inter-electrode distance). This will also set the mask to be polygonal based on the convex hull of the sensors.

  • 'head' (default for non-MEG sensors)

    Extrapolate out to the edges of the clipping circle. This will be on the head circle when the sensors are contained within the head circle, but it can extend beyond the head when sensors are plotted outside the head circle.

border.description: Value to extrapolate to on the topomap borders. If 'mean' (default), then each extrapolated point has the average value of its neighbours.

res.description: The resolution of the topomap image (number of pixels along each side).

vlim.description:
Lower and upper bounds of the colormap, typically a numeric value in the same units as the data. Elements of the :class:`tuple` may also be callable functions which take in a :class:`NumPy array <numpy.ndarray>` and return a scalar.

If both entries are None, the bounds are set at ± the maximum absolute value of the data (yielding a colormap with midpoint at 0), or (0, max(abs(data))) if the (possibly baselined) data are all-positive. Providing None for just one entry will set the corresponding boundary at the min/max of the data. If vlim="joint", will compute the colormap limits jointly across all topomaps of the same channel type (instead of separately for each topomap), using the min/max of the data for that channel type. Defaults to (None, None).

units.description: The units to use for the colorbar label. Ignored if colorbar=False. If None the label will be "AU" indicating arbitrary units. Default is None.

spatial_colors.description: Whether to color spectrum lines by channel location. Ignored if average=True.

exclude.description: Channel names to exclude from being drawn. If 'bads', channels in spectrum.info['bads'] are excluded; pass an empty list to include all channels (including "bad" channels, if any).

SpectrumArray.plot.description: Separate plots are drawn for each channel type. The line noise frequency is also indicated with a dashed line (⋮). If average=False, the plot will be interactive, and click-dragging on the spectrum will generate a scalp topography plot for the chosen frequency range in a new figure.

dB.description: Whether to plot on a decibel scale. If True, plots 10 × log₁₀(spectral_power/Hz).

color.description: A matplotlib-compatible color to use for the curves. Defaults to white.

fig_facecolor.description: A matplotlib-compatible color to use for the figure background. Defaults to black.

SpectrumArray.plot_topo.description: Plot power spectral density, separately for each channel.

bands.description:
The frequencies or frequency ranges to plot. If a :class:`dict`, keys will be used as subplot titles and values should be either a single frequency (e.g., {'presentation rate': 6.5}) or a length-two sequence of lower and upper frequency band edges (e.g., {'theta': (4, 8)}). If a single frequency is provided, the plot will show the frequency bin that is closest to the requested value. If None (the default), expands to:

bands = {'Delta (0-4 Hz)': (0, 4), 'Theta (4-8 Hz)': (4, 8),
         'Alpha (8-12 Hz)': (8, 12), 'Beta (12-30 Hz)': (12, 30),
         'Gamma (30-45 Hz)': (30, 45)}

Note

For backwards compatibility, :class:`tuples<tuple>` of length 2 or 3 are also accepted, where the last element of the tuple is the subplot title and the other entries are frequency values (a single value or band edges). New code should use :class:`dict` or None.

ch_type.description: The channel type to plot. For 'grad', the gradiometers are collected in pairs and the mean for each pair is plotted. If None the first available channel type from order shown above is used. Defaults to None.

normalize.description: If True, each band will be divided by the total power. Defaults to False.

agg_fun.description: The function used to aggregate over frequencies. Defaults to :func:`numpy.sum` if normalize=True, else :func:`numpy.mean`.

dB.description: Whether to plot on a decibel scale. If True, plots 10 × log₁₀(spectral_power/Hz), following the application of agg_fun. Ignored if normalize=True.

sensors.description: Whether to add markers for sensor locations. If :class:`str`, should be a valid matplotlib format string (e.g., 'r+' for red plusses, see the Notes section of :meth:`~matplotlib.axes.Axes.plot`). If True (the default), black circles will be used.

show_names.description: If True, show channel names next to each sensor marker. If callable, channel names will be formatted using the callable; e.g., to delete the prefix 'MEG ' from all channel names, pass the function lambda x: x.replace('MEG ', ''). If mask is not None, only non-masked sensor names will be shown.

mask.description: Array indicating channel-time combinations to highlight with a distinct plotting style (useful for, e.g. marking which channels at which times a statistical test of the data reaches significance). Array elements set to True will be plotted with the parameters given in mask_params. Defaults to None, equivalent to an array of all False elements.

mask_params.description:
Additional plotting parameters for plotting significant sensors. Default (None) equals:

dict(marker='o', markerfacecolor='w', markeredgecolor='k',
        linewidth=0, markersize=4)

contours.description: The number of contour lines to draw. If 0, no contours will be drawn. If a positive integer, that number of contour levels are chosen using the matplotlib tick locator (may sometimes be inaccurate, use array for accuracy). If array-like, the array values are used as the contour levels. The values should be in µV for EEG, fT for magnetometers and fT/m for gradiometers. If colorbar=True, the colorbar will have ticks corresponding to the contour levels. Default is 6.

outlines.description: The outlines to be drawn. If 'head', the default head scheme will be drawn. If dict, each key refers to a tuple of x and y positions, the values in 'mask_pos' will serve as image mask. Alternatively, a matplotlib patch object can be passed for advanced masking options, either directly or as a function that returns patches (required for multi-axis plots). If None, nothing will be drawn. Defaults to 'head'.

image_interp.description: The image interpolation to be used. Options are 'cubic' (default) to use :class:`scipy.interpolate.CloughTocher2DInterpolator`, 'nearest' to use :class:`scipy.spatial.Voronoi` or 'linear' to use :class:`scipy.interpolate.LinearNDInterpolator`.

extrapolate.description:
Options:

  • 'box'

    Extrapolate to four points placed to form a square encompassing all data points, where each side of the square is three times the range of the data in the respective dimension.

  • 'local' (default for MEG sensors)

    Extrapolate only to nearby points (approximately to points closer than median inter-electrode distance). This will also set the mask to be polygonal based on the convex hull of the sensors.

  • 'head' (default for non-MEG sensors)

    Extrapolate out to the edges of the clipping circle. This will be on the head circle when the sensors are contained within the head circle, but it can extend beyond the head when sensors are plotted outside the head circle.

border.description: Value to extrapolate to on the topomap borders. If 'mean' (default), then each extrapolated point has the average value of its neighbours.

res.description: The resolution of the topomap image (number of pixels along each side).

size.description: Side length of each subplot in inches.

vlim.description:
Lower and upper bounds of the colormap, typically a numeric value in the same units as the data. Elements of the :class:`tuple` may also be callable functions which take in a :class:`NumPy array <numpy.ndarray>` and return a scalar.

If both entries are None, the bounds are set at ± the maximum absolute value of the data (yielding a colormap with midpoint at 0), or (0, max(abs(data))) if the (possibly baselined) data are all-positive. Providing None for just one entry will set the corresponding boundary at the min/max of the data. If vlim="joint", will compute the colormap limits jointly across all topomaps of the same channel type (instead of separately for each topomap), using the min/max of the data for that channel type. Defaults to (None, None).

colorbar.description: Plot a colorbar in the rightmost column of the figure.

cbar_fmt.description: Formatting string for colorbar tick labels. See :ref:`formatspec` for details. If 'auto', is equivalent to '%0.3f' if dB=False and '%0.1f' if dB=True. Defaults to 'auto'.

units.description: The units to use for the colorbar label. Ignored if colorbar=False. If None the label will be "AU" indicating arbitrary units. Default is None.

dB.description: Whether to plot on a decibel scale. If True, plots 10 × log₁₀(spectral_power/Hz), following the application of agg_fun. Ignored if normalize=True.

sensors.description: Whether to add markers for sensor locations. If :class:`str`, should be a valid matplotlib format string (e.g., 'r+' for red plusses, see the Notes section of :meth:`~matplotlib.axes.Axes.plot`). If True (the default), black circles will be used.

show_names.description: If True, show channel names next to each sensor marker. If callable, channel names will be formatted using the callable; e.g., to delete the prefix 'MEG ' from all channel names, pass the function lambda x: x.replace('MEG ', ''). If mask is not None, only non-masked sensor names will be shown.

mask.description: Array indicating channel-time combinations to highlight with a distinct plotting style (useful for, e.g. marking which channels at which times a statistical test of the data reaches significance). Array elements set to True will be plotted with the parameters given in mask_params. Defaults to None, equivalent to an array of all False elements.

mask_params.description:
Additional plotting parameters for plotting significant sensors. Default (None) equals:

dict(marker='o', markerfacecolor='w', markeredgecolor='k',
        linewidth=0, markersize=4)

contours.description: The number of contour lines to draw. If 0, no contours will be drawn. If a positive integer, that number of contour levels are chosen using the matplotlib tick locator (may sometimes be inaccurate, use array for accuracy). If array-like, the array values are used as the contour levels. The values should be in µV for EEG, fT for magnetometers and fT/m for gradiometers. If colorbar=True, the colorbar will have ticks corresponding to the contour levels. Default is 6.

outlines.description: The outlines to be drawn. If 'head', the default head scheme will be drawn. If dict, each key refers to a tuple of x and y positions, the values in 'mask_pos' will serve as image mask. Alternatively, a matplotlib patch object can be passed for advanced masking options, either directly or as a function that returns patches (required for multi-axis plots). If None, nothing will be drawn. Defaults to 'head'.

image_interp.description: The image interpolation to be used. Options are 'cubic' (default) to use :class:`scipy.interpolate.CloughTocher2DInterpolator`, 'nearest' to use :class:`scipy.spatial.Voronoi` or 'linear' to use :class:`scipy.interpolate.LinearNDInterpolator`.

extrapolate.description:
Options:

  • 'box'

    Extrapolate to four points placed to form a square encompassing all data points, where each side of the square is three times the range of the data in the respective dimension.

  • 'local' (default for MEG sensors)

    Extrapolate only to nearby points (approximately to points closer than median inter-electrode distance). This will also set the mask to be polygonal based on the convex hull of the sensors.

  • 'head' (default for non-MEG sensors)

    Extrapolate out to the edges of the clipping circle. This will be on the head circle when the sensors are contained within the head circle, but it can extend beyond the head when sensors are plotted outside the head circle.

border.description: Value to extrapolate to on the topomap borders. If 'mean' (default), then each extrapolated point has the average value of its neighbours.

res.description: The resolution of the topomap image (number of pixels along each side).

size.description: Side length of each subplot in inches.

vlim.description:
Lower and upper bounds of the colormap, typically a numeric value in the same units as the data. Elements of the :class:`tuple` may also be callable functions which take in a :class:`NumPy array <numpy.ndarray>` and return a scalar.

If both entries are None, the bounds are set at ± the maximum absolute value of the data (yielding a colormap with midpoint at 0), or (0, max(abs(data))) if the (possibly baselined) data are all-positive. Providing None for just one entry will set the corresponding boundary at the min/max of the data. If vlim="joint", will compute the colormap limits jointly across all topomaps of the same channel type (instead of separately for each topomap), using the min/max of the data for that channel type. Defaults to (None, None).

units.description: The units to use for the colorbar label. Ignored if colorbar=False. If None the label will be "AU" indicating arbitrary units. Default is None.

tfr_array_morlet.description: Same computation as ~mne.time_frequency.tfr_morlet, but operates on :class:`NumPy arrays <numpy.ndarray>` instead of ~mne.Epochs objects.

sfreq.description: Sampling frequency of the data in Hz.

n_cycles.description: Number of cycles in the wavelet, either a fixed number or one per frequency. The number of cycles n_cycles and the frequencies of interest freqs define the temporal window length. See notes for additional information about the relationship between those arguments and about time and frequency smoothing.

zero_mean.description: If True, make sure the wavelets have a mean of zero. Defaults to True.

use_fft.description: Use the FFT for convolutions or not. Defaults to True.

decim.description:
Decimation factor, applied after time-frequency decomposition.

  • if :class:`int`, returns tfr[..., ::decim] (keep only every Nth sample along the time axis).

  • if :class:`slice`, returns tfr[..., decim] (keep only the specified slice along the time axis).

Note

Decimation is done after convolutions and may create aliasing artifacts.

output.description:
• 'complex' : single trial per taper complex values.

  • 'power' : single trial power.

  • 'phase' : single trial per taper phase.

  • 'avg_power' : average of single trial power.

  • 'itc' : inter-trial coherence.

  • 'avg_power_itc' : average of single trial power and inter-trial coherence across trials.

n_jobs.description: The number of jobs to run in parallel. If -1, it is set to the number of CPU cores. Requires the :mod:`joblib` package. None (default) is a marker for 'unset' that will be interpreted as n_jobs=1 (sequential execution) unless the call is performed under a :class:`joblib:joblib.parallel_config` context manager that sets another value for n_jobs. The parallelization is implemented across channels.

return_weights.description: If True, return the taper weights. Only applies if output='complex' or 'phase'.

verbose.description: Control verbosity of the logging output. If None, use the default verbosity level. See the :ref:`logging documentation <tut-logging>` and :func:`mne.verbose` for details. Should only be passed as a keyword argument.

tfr_array_multitaper.description: Same computation as ~mne.time_frequency.tfr_multitaper, but operates on :class:`NumPy arrays <numpy.ndarray>` instead of ~mne.Epochs or ~mne.Evoked objects.

fmin.description: The minimum frequency to include. If None defaults to the minimum fft frequency greater than zero.

fmax.description: The maximum frequency to include. If None defaults to the maximum fft.

n_fft.description: The length of the windows used for FFT. If None, it defaults to the next power of 2 larger than the signal length.

width.description: The width of the Gaussian window. If < 1, increased temporal resolution, if > 1, increased frequency resolution. Defaults to 1. (classical S-Transform).

decim.description:
Decimation factor, applied after time-frequency decomposition.

  • if :class:`int`, returns tfr[..., ::decim] (keep only every Nth sample along the time axis).

  • if :class:`slice`, returns tfr[..., decim] (keep only the specified slice along the time axis).

Note

Decimation is done after convolutions and may create aliasing artifacts.

return_itc.description: Return intertrial coherence (ITC) as well as averaged power.

n_jobs.description: The number of jobs to run in parallel. If -1, it is set to the number of CPU cores. Requires the :mod:`joblib` package. None (default) is a marker for 'unset' that will be interpreted as n_jobs=1 (sequential execution) unless the call is performed under a :class:`joblib:joblib.parallel_config` context manager that sets another value for n_jobs.

verbose.description: Control verbosity of the logging output. If None, use the default verbosity level. See the :ref:`logging documentation <tut-logging>` and :func:`mne.verbose` for details. Should only be passed as a keyword argument.

tfr_array_stockwell.description:
Same computation as ~mne.time_frequency.tfr_stockwell, but operates on :class:`NumPy arrays <numpy.ndarray>` instead of ~mne.Epochs objects.

See :footcite:`Stockwell2007,MoukademEtAl2014,WheatEtAl2010,JonesEtAl2006` for more information.

X.description: The signals.

use_fft.description: Use FFT for convolutions. Defaults to True.

mode.description: Convention for convolution. 'full' is currently not implemented with use_fft=False. Defaults to 'same'.

decim.description:
Decimation factor, applied after time-frequency decomposition.

  • if :class:`int`, returns tfr[..., ::decim] (keep only every Nth sample along the time axis).

  • if :class:`slice`, returns tfr[..., decim] (keep only the specified slice along the time axis).

Note

Decimation is done after convolutions and may create aliasing artifacts.

cwt.description: Compute time-frequency decomposition with continuous wavelet transform.

subject.description: Subject name in Freesurfer subjects dir.

hemi.description: Hemisphere id (ie 'lh', 'rh', 'both', or 'split'). In the case of 'both', both hemispheres are shown in the same window. In the case of 'split' hemispheres are displayed side-by-side in different viewing panes.

title.description: Title for the window.

cortex.description:
Specifies how the cortical surface is rendered. Options:

  1. The name of one of the preset cortex styles:

    'classic' (default), 'high_contrast', 'low_contrast', or 'bone'.

  2. A single color-like argument to render the cortex as a single

    color, e.g. 'red' or (0.1, 0.4, 1.).

  3. A list of two color-like used to render binarized curvature

    values for gyral (first) and sulcal (second). regions, e.g., ['red', 'blue'] or [(1, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1)].

  4. A dict containing keys 'vmin', 'vmax', 'colormap' with

    values used to render the binarized curvature (where 0 is gyral, 1 is sulcal).

size.description: The size of the window, in pixels. can be one number to specify a square window, or a length-2 sequence to specify (width, height).

foreground.description: Color of the foreground (will be used for colorbars and text). None (default) will use black or white depending on the value of background.

subjects_dir.description: If not None, this directory will be used as the subjects directory instead of the value set using the SUBJECTS_DIR environment variable.

views.description: View to use. Using multiple views (list) is not supported for mpl backend. See :meth:`Brain.show_view <mne.viz.Brain.show_view>` for valid string options.

offset.description: If True, shifts the right- or left-most x coordinate of the left and right surfaces, respectively, to be at zero. This is useful for viewing inflated surface where hemispheres typically overlap. Can be "auto" (default) use True with inflated surfaces and False otherwise (Default: 'auto'). Only used when hemi='both'.

interaction.description: Can be "trackball" (default) or "terrain", i.e. a turntable-style camera.

units.description: Can be 'm' or 'mm' (default).

view_layout.description: Can be "vertical" (default) or "horizontal". When using "horizontal" mode, the PyVista backend must be used and hemi cannot be "split".

silhouette.description: As a dict, it contains the color, linewidth, alpha opacity and decimate (level of decimation between 0 and 1 or None) of the brain's silhouette to display. If True, the default values are used and if False, no silhouette will be displayed. Defaults to False.

theme.description: Can be "auto", "light", or "dark" or a path-like to a custom stylesheet. For Dark-Mode and automatic Dark-Mode-Detection, qdarkstyle and darkdetect, respectively, are required. If None (default), the config option MNE_3D_OPTION_THEME will be used, defaulting to "auto" if it's not found.

show.description: Display the window as soon as it is ready. Defaults to True.

time_viewer.description: If True, enable widgets interaction. Defaults to True.

show_traces.description: If True, enable visualization of time traces. Defaults to True.

value.description: If True, the widgets are shown and if False, they are hidden. If None, the state of the widgets is toggled. Defaults to None.
If True, automatic time playback is enabled and if False, it's disabled. If None, the state of time playback is toggled. Defaults to None.

Brain.plot_time_line.description: Add the time line to the MPL widget.

array.description: Data array. For the data to be understood as vector-valued (3 values per vertex corresponding to X/Y/Z surface RAS), then array must be have all 3 dimensions. If vectors with no time dimension are desired, consider using a singleton (e.g., np.newaxis) to create a "time" dimension and pass time_label=None (vector values are not supported).

fmin.description: Minimum value in colormap (uses real fmin if None).

fmid.description: Intermediate value in colormap (fmid between fmin and fmax if None).

fmax.description: Maximum value in colormap (uses real max if None).

thresh.description: Not supported yet. If not None, values below thresh will not be visible.

center.description: If not None, center of a divergent colormap, changes the meaning of fmin, fmax and fmid.

transparent.description: If True: use a linear transparency between fmin and fmid and make values below fmin fully transparent (symmetrically for divergent colormaps). None will choose automatically based on colormap type.

colormap.description: Name of matplotlib colormap to use, a list of matplotlib colors, or a custom look up table (an n x 4 array coded with RBGA values between 0 and 255), the default "auto" chooses a default divergent colormap, if "center" is given (currently "icefire"), otherwise a default sequential colormap (currently "rocket").

vertices.description: Vertices for which the data is defined (needed if len(data) < nvtx).

smoothing_steps.description: Number of smoothing steps (smoothing is used if len(data) < nvtx) The value 'nearest' can be used too. None (default) will use as many as necessary to fill the surface.

time.description: Time points in the data array (if data is 2D or 3D).

time_label.description: Format of the time label (a format string, a function that maps floating point time values to strings, or None for no label). The default is 'auto', which will use time=%0.2f ms if there is more than one time point.

colorbar.description: Whether to add a colorbar to the figure. Can also be a tuple to give the (row, col) index of where to put the colorbar.

hemi.description: If None, it is assumed to belong to the hemisphere being shown. If two hemispheres are being shown, an error will be thrown.

remove_existing.description: Not supported yet. Remove surface added by previous "add_data" call. Useful for conserving memory when displaying different data in a loop.

initial_time.description: Time initially shown in the plot. None to use the first time sample (default).

scale_factor.description: The scale factor to use when displaying glyphs for vector-valued data.

vector_alpha.description: Alpha level to control opacity of the arrows. Only used for vector-valued data. If None (default), alpha is used.

volume_options.description:
Options for volumetric source estimate plotting, with key/value pairs:

  • 'resolution'float | None

    Resolution (in mm) of volume rendering. Smaller (e.g., 1.) looks better at the cost of speed. None (default) uses the volume source space resolution, which is often something like 7 or 5 mm, without resampling.

  • 'blending'str

    Can be "mip" (default) for :term:`maximum intensity projection` or "composite" for composite blending using alpha values.

  • 'alpha'float | None

    Alpha for the volumetric rendering. Defaults are 0.4 for vector source estimates and 1.0 for scalar source estimates.

  • 'surface_alpha'float | None

    Alpha for the surface enclosing the volume(s). None (default) will use half the volume alpha. Set to zero to avoid plotting the surface.

  • 'silhouette_alpha'float | None

    Alpha for a silhouette along the outside of the volume. None (default) will use 0.25 * surface_alpha.

  • 'silhouette_linewidth'float

    The line width to use for the silhouette. Default is 2.

A float input (default 1.) or None will be used for the 'resolution' entry.

verbose.description: Control verbosity of the logging output. If None, use the default verbosity level. See the :ref:`logging documentation <tut-logging>` and :func:`mne.verbose` for details. Should only be passed as a keyword argument.

Brain.add_data.description:
This provides a similar interface to PySurfer, but it displays it with a single colormap. It offers more flexibility over the colormap, and provides a way to display four-dimensional data (i.e., a timecourse) or five-dimensional data (i.e., a vector-valued timecourse).

Note

fmin sets the low end of the colormap, and is separate from thresh (this is a different convention from PySurfer).

Brain.remove_labels.description: Remove all the ROI labels from the image.

scalar_thresh.description: Threshold the label ids using this value in the label file's scalar field (i.e. label only vertices with scalar >= thresh).

borders.description: Show only label borders. If int, specify the number of steps (away from the true border) along the cortical mesh to include as part of the border definition.

hemi.description: If None, it is assumed to belong to the hemisphere being shown.

subdir.description: If a label is specified as name, subdir can be used to indicate that the label file is in a sub-directory of the subject's label directory rather than in the label directory itself (e.g. for $SUBJECTS_DIR/$SUBJECT/label/aparc/lh.cuneus.label brain.add_label('cuneus', subdir='aparc')).

Brain.add_label.description: Add an ROI label to the image.

scale.description: The size of the arrow representing the dipoles in :class:`mne.viz.Brain` units. Default 1.5mm.

Brain.add_forward.description: Add a quiver to render positions of dipoles.

Brain.remove_forward.description: Remove forward sources from the rendered scene.

scales.description: The size of the arrow representing the dipole in :class:`mne.viz.Brain` units. Default 5mm.

mode.description: The drawing mode for the dipole to render. Defaults to "arrow".

Brain.add_dipole.description: Add a quiver to render positions of dipoles.

Brain.remove_dipole.description: Remove dipole objects from the rendered scene.

dense.description: Whether to plot the dense head (seghead) or the less dense head (head).

color.description: A list of anything matplotlib accepts: string, RGB, hex, etc.

Brain.add_head.description: Add a mesh to render the outer head surface.

Brain.remove_head.description: Remove head objects from the rendered scene.

outer.description: Adds the outer skull if True, otherwise adds the inner skull.

color.description: A list of anything matplotlib accepts: string, RGB, hex, etc.

Brain.add_skull.description: Add a mesh to render the skull surface.

Brain.remove_skull.description: Remove skull objects from the rendered scene.

aseg.description: The anatomical segmentation file. Default auto uses aparc+aseg if available and wmparc if not. This may be any anatomical segmentation file in the mri subdirectory of the Freesurfer subject directory.

labels.description: Labeled regions of interest to plot. See :func:`mne.get_montage_volume_labels` for one way to determine regions of interest. Regions can also be chosen from the :term:`FreeSurfer LUT`.

fill_hole_size.description: The size of holes to remove in the mesh in voxels. Default is None, no holes are removed. Warning, this dilates the boundaries of the surface by fill_hole_size number of voxels so use the minimal size.

legend.description: Add a legend displaying the names of the labels. Default (None) is True if the number of labels is 10 or fewer. Can also be a dict of kwargs to pass to pyvista.Plotter.add_legend.

Brain.add_volume_labels.description: Add labels to the rendering from an anatomical segmentation.

Brain.remove_volume_labels.description: Remove the volume labels from the rendered scene.

coords.description: Coordinates in stereotaxic space (default) or array of vertex ids (with coord_as_verts=True).

coords_as_verts.description: Whether the coords parameter should be interpreted as vertex ids.

map_surface.description: Surface to project the coordinates to, or None to use raw coords. When set to a surface, each foci is positioned at the closest vertex in the mesh.

scale_factor.description: Controls the size of the foci spheres (relative to 1cm).

color.description: A list of anything matplotlib accepts: string, RGB, hex, etc.

hemi.description: If None, it is assumed to belong to the hemisphere being shown. If two hemispheres are being shown, an error will be thrown.

Brain.add_foci.description: The foci spheres can be displayed at the coordinates given, or mapped through a surface geometry. In other words, coordinates from a volume-based analysis in MNI space can be displayed on an inflated average surface by finding the closest vertex on the white surface and mapping to that vertex on the inflated mesh.

meg.description: Can be "helmet", "sensors" or "ref" to show the MEG helmet, sensors or reference sensors respectively, or a combination like ('helmet', 'sensors') (same as None, default). True translates to ('helmet', 'sensors', 'ref'). Can also be a dict to specify alpha values, e.g. {"helmet": 0.1, "sensors": 0.8}.

eeg.description:
String options are:

  • "original" (default; equivalent to True)

    Shows EEG sensors using their digitized locations (after transformation to the chosen coord_frame)

  • "projected"

    The EEG locations projected onto the scalp, as is done in forward modeling

Can also be a list of these options, or a dict to specify the alpha values to use, e.g. dict(original=0.2, projected=0.8).

fnirs.description: Can be "channels", "pairs", "detectors", and/or "sources" to show the fNIRS channel locations, optode locations, or line between source-detector pairs, or a combination like ('pairs', 'channels'). True translates to ('pairs',). A dict can also be used to specify alpha values (but only "channels" and "pairs" will be used), e.g. dict(channels=0.2, pairs=0.7).

dbs.description: If True (default), show DBS (deep brain stimulation) electrodes.

max_dist.description: The maximum distance to project a sensor to the pial surface in meters. Sensors that are greater than this distance from the pial surface will not be assigned locations. Projections can be done to the inflated or flat brain.

sensor_colors.description:
Colors to use for the sensor glyphs. Can be None (default) to use default colors. A dict should provide the colors (values) for each channel type (keys), e.g.:

dict(eeg=eeg_colors)

Where the value (eeg_colors above) can be broadcast to an array of colors with length that matches the number of channels of that type, i.e., is compatible with :func:`matplotlib.colors.to_rgba_array`. A few examples of this for the case above are the string "k", a list of n_eeg color strings, or an NumPy ndarray of shape (n_eeg, 3) or (n_eeg, 4).

sensor_scales.description:
Scale to use for the sensor glyphs. Can be None (default) to use default scale. A dict should provide the Scale (values) for each channel type (keys), e.g.:

dict(eeg=eeg_scales)

Where the value (eeg_scales above) can be broadcast to an array of values with length that matches the number of channels of that type. A few examples of this for the case above are the value 10e-3, a list of n_eeg values, or an NumPy ndarray of shape (n_eeg,).

verbose.description: Control verbosity of the logging output. If None, use the default verbosity level. See the :ref:`logging documentation <tut-logging>` and :func:`mne.verbose` for details. Should only be passed as a keyword argument.

name.description: Remove specific text by name. If None, all text will be removed.

borders.description: Show only label borders. If int, specify the number of steps (away from the true border) along the cortical mesh to include as part of the border definition.

imdata.description: The image that you wish to click on for 2-d points.

Takes as input an image array (can be any array that works with imshow, but will work best with images. Displays the image and lets you click on it. Stores the xy coordinates of each click, so now you can superimpose something on top of it.

Upon clicking, the x/y coordinate of the cursor will be stored in self.coords, which is a list of (x, y) tuples.

set_ratios.description: Set the aspect ratio of any axes in fig to the value in set_ratios. Defaults to None, which does nothing to axes.

add_background_image.description:
Adds the image specified in im to the figure fig. This is generally meant to be done with topo plots, though it could work for any plot.

Note

This modifies the figure and/or axes in place.

fname_out.description: Filename to store the resulting diff. If None, a temporary file will be created.

show.description: If True, show the resulting diff in a new tab in a web browser.

read_limit.description: Max number of bytes of data to read from a tag. Can be np.inf to always read all data (helps test read completion).

max_str.description: Max number of characters of string representation to print for each tag's data.

verbose.description: Control verbosity of the logging output. If None, use the default verbosity level. See the :ref:`logging documentation <tut-logging>` and :func:`mne.verbose` for details. Should only be passed as a keyword argument.

compare_fiff.description: Compare the contents of two fiff files using diff and show_fiff.

node_order.description: List with node names defining the order in which the nodes are arranged. Must have the elements as node_names but the order can be different. The nodes are arranged clockwise starting at "start_pos" degrees.

start_pos.description: Angle in degrees that defines where the first node is plotted.

start_between.description: If True, the layout starts with the position between the nodes. This is the same as adding "180. / len(node_names)" to start_pos.

group_boundaries.description: List of of boundaries between groups at which point a "group_sep" will be inserted. E.g. "[0, len(node_names) / 2]" will create two groups.

circular_layout.description: Create layout arranging nodes on a circle.

on_pick.description: The callback function to be invoked on clicking one of the axes. Is supposed to instantiate the following API: function(axis, channel_index).

fig_facecolor.description: The figure face color. Defaults to black.

axis_facecolor.description: The axis face color. Defaults to black.

axis_spinecolor.description: The axis spine color. Defaults to black. In other words, the color of the axis' edge lines.

layout_scale.description: Scaling factor for adjusting the relative size of the layout on the canvas. If None, nothing will be scaled.

legend.description: If True, an additional axis is created in the bottom right corner that can be used to, e.g., construct a legend. The index of this axis will be -1.

select.description: Whether to enable the lasso-selection tool to enable the user to select channels. The selected channels will be available in fig.lasso.selection.

iter_topography.description: This function returns a generator that unpacks into a series of matplotlib axis objects and data / channel indices, both corresponding to the sensor positions of the related layout passed or inferred from the channel info. Hence, this enables convenient topography plot customization.

format.description: Type of colormap to return. If 'matplotlib', will return a matplotlib.colors.LinearSegmentedColormap. If 'vtk', will return an RGBA array of shape (256, 4).

mne_analyze_colormap.description: Return a colormap similar to that used by mne_analyze.

subject.description: The FreeSurfer subject name.

subjects_dir.description: The path to the directory containing the FreeSurfer subjects reconstructions. If None, defaults to the SUBJECTS_DIR environment variable.

slices.description: The indices of the MRI slices to plot. If None, automatically pick 12 equally-spaced slices.

brain_surfaces.description: One or more brain surface to plot (optional). Entries should correspond to files in the subject's surf directory (e.g. "white").

mri.description: The name of the MRI to use. Can be a standard FreeSurfer MRI such as 'T1.mgz', or a full path to a custom MRI file.

show_orientation.description: Show the orientation (L/R, P/A, I/S) of the data slices. True (default) will only show it on the outside most edges of the figure, False will never show labels, and "always" will label each plot.

plot_bem.description: Plot BEM contours on anatomical MRI slices.

clim.description:
Colorbar properties specification. If 'auto', set clim automatically based on data percentiles. If dict, should contain:

kind'value' | 'percent'

Flag to specify type of limits.

limslist | np.ndarray | tuple of float, 3 elements

Lower, middle, and upper bounds for colormap.

pos_limslist | np.ndarray | tuple of float, 3 elements

Lower, middle, and upper bound for colormap. Positive values will be mirrored directly across zero during colormap construction to obtain negative control points.

Note

Only one of lims or pos_lims should be provided. Only sequential colormaps should be used with lims, and only divergent colormaps should be used with pos_lims.

transparent.description: If True: use a linear transparency between fmin and fmid and make values below fmin fully transparent (symmetrically for divergent colormaps). None will choose automatically based on colormap type.

orientation.description: Orientation of the colorbar, can be "vertical" or "horizontal".

bgcolor.description: The color behind the colorbar (for alpha blending).

plot_brain_colorbar.description: Plot a colorbar that corresponds to a brain activation map.

bridged_idx.description: The indices of channels marked as bridged with each bridged pair stored as a tuple. Can be generated via :func:`mne.preprocessing.compute_bridged_electrodes`.

ed_matrix.description: The electrical distance matrix for each pair of EEG electrodes. Can be generated via :func:`mne.preprocessing.compute_bridged_electrodes`.

title.description: A title to add to the plot.

plot_bridged_electrodes.description: Topoplot electrode distance matrix with bridged electrodes connected.

snr_dict.description: The dictionary returned by ~mne.chpi.compute_chpi_snr. Must have keys times, freqs, TYPE_snr, TYPE_power, and TYPE_resid (where TYPE can be mag or grad or both).

plot_chpi_snr.description: Plot time-varying SNR estimates of the HPI coils.

exclude.description: List of channels to exclude. If empty do not exclude any channel. If 'bads', exclude info['bads'].

colorbar.description: Show colorbar or not.

proj.description: Apply projections or not.

show_svd.description: Plot also singular values of the noise covariance for each sensor type. We show square roots ie. standard deviations.

verbose.description: Control verbosity of the logging output. If None, use the default verbosity level. See the :ref:`logging documentation <tut-logging>` and :func:`mne.verbose` for details. Should only be passed as a keyword argument.

labels.description: Lists of labels (values) associated with each channel (keys).

picks.description: The channels to consider.

plot_channel_labels_circle.description:
Note

This primarily makes sense for sEEG channels where each channel can be assigned an anatomical label as the electrode passes through various brain areas.

adjacency.description: Array of channels x channels shape. Defines which channels are adjacent to each other. Note that if you edit adjacencies (via edit=True), this array will be modified in place.

ch_names.description: Names of successive channels in the adjacency matrix.

kind.description: How to plot the adjacency. Can be either '3d' or '2d'.

edit.description: Whether to allow interactive editing of the adjacency matrix via clicking respective channel pairs. Once clicked, the channel is "activated" and turns green. Clicking on another channel adds or removes adjacency relation between the activated and newly clicked channel (depending on whether the channels are already adjacent or not); the newly clicked channel now becomes activated. Clicking on an activated channel deactivates it. Editing is currently only supported for kind='2d'.

mode.description: Whether to plot the cross-spectral density ('csd', the default), or the coherence ('coh') between the channels.

colorbar.description: Whether to show a colorbar. Defaults to True.

cmap.description: The matplotlib colormap to use. Defaults to None, which means the colormap will default to matplotlib's default.

n_cols.description: CSD matrices are plotted in a grid. This parameter controls how many matrix to plot side by side before starting a new row. By default, a number will be chosen to make the grid as square as possible.

show.description: Whether to show the figure. Defaults to True.

plot_csd.description: A sub-plot is created for each frequency. If an info object is passed to the function, different channel types are plotted in different figures.

colors.description: Color to plot with each dipole. If None default colors are used.

plot_dipole_amplitudes.description: Plot the amplitude traces of a set of dipoles.

trans.description: The mri to head trans. Can be None with mode set to '3d'.

subject.description: The FreeSurfer subject name (will be used to set the FreeSurfer environment variable SUBJECT). Can be None with mode set to '3d'.

subjects_dir.description: The path to the directory containing the FreeSurfer subjects reconstructions. If None, defaults to the SUBJECTS_DIR environment variable.

mode.description:
Can be:

'arrow' or 'sphere'

Plot in 3D mode using PyVista with the given glyph type.

'orthoview'

Plot in matplotlib Axes3D using matplotlib with MRI slices shown on the sides of a cube, with the dipole(s) shown as arrows extending outward from a dot (i.e., the arrows pivot on the tail).

'outlines'

Plot in matplotlib Axes using a quiver of arrows for the dipoles in three axes (axial, coronal, and sagittal views), with the arrow pivoting in the middle of the arrow.

coord_frame.description: Coordinate frame to use: 'head' or 'mri'. Can also be 'mri_rotated' when mode equals 'outlines'. Defaults to 'mri'.

idx.description: Index of the initially plotted dipole. Can also be 'gof' to plot the dipole with highest goodness of fit value or 'amplitude' to plot the dipole with the highest amplitude. The dipoles can also be browsed through using up/down arrow keys or mouse scroll. Defaults to 'gof'. Only used if mode equals 'orthoview'.

show_all.description: Whether to always plot all the dipoles. If True (default), the active dipole is plotted as a red dot and its location determines the shown MRI slices. The non-active dipoles are plotted as small blue dots. If False, only the active dipole is plotted. Only used if mode='orthoview'.

block.description: Whether to halt program execution until the figure is closed. Defaults to False. Only used if mode equals 'orthoview'.

show.description: Show figure if True. Defaults to True. Only used if mode equals 'orthoview'.

scale.description: The scale (size in meters) of the dipoles if mode is not 'orthoview'. The default is 0.03 when mode is 'outlines' and 0.005 otherwise.

color.description: The color of the dipoles. The default (None) will use 'y' if mode is 'orthoview' and show_all is True, else 'r'. Can also be a list of colors to use when mode is 'outlines'.

highlight_color.description: The highlight color. Only used in orthoview mode with show_all=True.

title.description: The title of the figure if mode='orthoview' (ignored for all other modes). If None, dipole number and its properties (amplitude, orientation etc.) will be shown. Defaults to None.

head_source.description: Head source(s) to use. See the source option of :func:`mne.get_head_surf` for more information. Only used when mode equals 'outlines'.

surf.description: Brain surface to show outlines for, can be 'white', 'pial', or None. Only used when mode is 'outlines'.

width.description: Width of the matplotlib quiver arrow, see :meth:`matplotlib:matplotlib.axes.Axes.quiver`. If None (default), when mode is 'outlines' 0.015 will be used, and when mode is 'orthoview' the matplotlib default is used.

verbose.description: Control verbosity of the logging output. If None, use the default verbosity level. See the :ref:`logging documentation <tut-logging>` and :func:`mne.verbose` for details. Should only be passed as a keyword argument.

plot_dipole_locations.description: If mode is set to 'arrow' or 'sphere', only the location of the first time point of each dipole is shown else use the show_all parameter.

threshold.description: The percentage threshold to use to decide whether or not to plot. Default is zero (always plot).

n_max_plot.description: Maximum number of channels to show stats for.

subject.description: The subject name to use in the title of the plot. If None, do not display a subject name.

color.description: Color to use for the bars.

plot_drop_log.description: Show the channel stats based on a drop_log from Epochs.

picks.description: Channels to include. Slices and lists of integers will be interpreted as channel indices. In lists, channel type strings (e.g., ['meg', 'eeg']) will pick channels of those types, channel name strings (e.g., ['MEG0111', 'MEG2623'] will pick the given channels. Can also be the string values 'all' to pick all channels, or 'data' to pick :term:`data channels`. None (default) will pick good data channels. Note that channels in info['bads'] will be included if their names or indices are explicitly provided.

scalings.description:
Scaling factors for the traces. If a dictionary where any value is 'auto', the scaling factor is set to match the 99.5th percentile of the respective data. If 'auto', all scalings (for all channel types) are set to 'auto'. If any values are 'auto' and the data is not preloaded, a subset up to 100 MB will be loaded. If None, defaults to:

dict(mag=1e-12, grad=4e-11, eeg=20e-6, eog=150e-6, ecg=5e-4,
     emg=1e-3, ref_meg=1e-12, misc=1e-3, stim=1,
     resp=1, chpi=1e-4, whitened=1e2)

Note

A particular scaling value s corresponds to half of the visualized signal range around zero (i.e. from 0 to +s or from 0 to -s). For example, the default scaling of 20e-6 (20µV) for EEG signals means that the visualized range will be 40 µV (20 µV in the positive direction and 20 µV in the negative direction).

n_epochs.description: The number of epochs per view. Defaults to 20.

n_channels.description: The number of channels per view. Defaults to 20.

title.description: The title of the window. If None, the event names (from epochs.event_id) will be displayed. Defaults to None.

event_color.description: Color(s) to use for :term:`events`. To show all :term:`events` in the same color, pass any matplotlib-compatible color. To color events differently, pass a dict that maps event names or integer event numbers to colors (must include entries for all events, or include a "fallback" entry with key -1). If None, colors are chosen from the current Matplotlib color cycle. Defaults to None.

order.description: Order in which to plot data. If the array is shorter than the number of channels, only the given channels are plotted. If None (default), all channels are plotted. If group_by is 'position' or 'selection', the order parameter is used only for selecting the channels to be plotted.

show.description: Show figure if True. Defaults to True.

block.description: Whether to halt program execution until the figure is closed. Useful for rejecting bad trials on the fly by clicking on an epoch. Defaults to False.

decim.description: Amount to decimate the data during display for speed purposes. You should only decimate if the data are sufficiently low-passed, otherwise aliasing can occur. The 'auto' mode (default) uses the decimation that results in a sampling rate at least three times larger than info['lowpass'] (e.g., a 40 Hz lowpass will result in at least a 120 Hz displayed sample rate).

butterfly.description: Whether to directly call the butterfly view.

show_scrollbars.description: Whether to show scrollbars when the plot is initialized. Can be toggled after initialization by pressing :kbd:`z` ("zen mode") while the plot window is focused. Default is True.

show_scalebars.description: Whether to show scale bars when the plot is initialized. Can be toggled after initialization by pressing :kbd:`s` while the plot window is focused. Default is True.

group_by.description: How to group channels. 'type' groups by channel type, 'original' plots in the order of ch_names, 'selection' uses Elekta's channel groupings (only works for Neuromag data), 'position' groups the channels by the positions of the sensors. 'selection' and 'position' modes allow custom selections by using a lasso selector on the topomap. In butterfly mode, 'type' and 'original' group the channels by type, whereas 'selection' and 'position' use regional grouping. 'type' and 'original' modes are ignored when order is not None. Defaults to 'type'.

precompute.description: Whether to load all data (not just the visible portion) into RAM and apply preprocessing (e.g., projectors) to the full data array in a separate processor thread, instead of window-by-window during scrolling. The default None uses the MNE_BROWSER_PRECOMPUTE variable, which defaults to 'auto'. 'auto' compares available RAM space to the expected size of the precomputed data, and precomputes only if enough RAM is available. This is only used with the Qt backend.

use_opengl.description: Whether to use OpenGL when rendering the plot (requires pyopengl). May increase performance, but effect is dependent on system CPU and graphics hardware. Only works if using the Qt backend. Default is None, which will use False unless the user configuration variable MNE_BROWSER_USE_OPENGL is set to 'true', see :func:`mne.set_config`.

theme.description: Can be "auto", "light", or "dark" or a path-like to a custom stylesheet. For Dark-Mode and automatic Dark-Mode-Detection, qdarkstyle and darkdetect, respectively, are required. If None (default), the config option MNE_BROWSER_THEME will be used, defaulting to "auto" if it's not found. For the "matplotlib" backend, only "light", "dark", and "auto" are supported. For the "qt" backend, a path-like to a custom stylesheet is also accepted.

overview_mode.description: Can be "channels", "empty", or "hidden" to set the overview bar mode for the 'qt' backend. If None (default), the config option MNE_BROWSER_OVERVIEW_MODE will be used, defaulting to "channels" if it's not found.

splash.description: If True (default), a splash screen is shown during the application startup. Only applicable to the qt backend.

annotation_colors.description: A dictionary mapping annotation description strings to colors. Use this to override the default color assigned to specific annotation types (e.g., dict(bad_segment='orange')). Colors can be any valid Matplotlib color specification. Keys that do not match any annotation description in the data will trigger a warning. If None (default), automatic colors are used.

plot_epochs.description: Bad epochs can be marked with a left click on top of the epoch. Bad channels can be selected by clicking the channel name on the left side of the main axes. Calling this function drops all the selected bad epochs as well as bad epochs marked beforehand with rejection parameters.

bands.description:
The frequencies or frequency ranges to plot. If a :class:`dict`, keys will be used as subplot titles and values should be either a single frequency (e.g., {'presentation rate': 6.5}) or a length-two sequence of lower and upper frequency band edges (e.g., {'theta': (4, 8)}). If a single frequency is provided, the plot will show the frequency bin that is closest to the requested value. If None (the default), expands to:

bands = {'Delta (0-4 Hz)': (0, 4), 'Theta (4-8 Hz)': (4, 8),
         'Alpha (8-12 Hz)': (8, 12), 'Beta (12-30 Hz)': (12, 30),
         'Gamma (30-45 Hz)': (30, 45)}

Note

For backwards compatibility, :class:`tuples<tuple>` of length 2 or 3 are also accepted, where the last element of the tuple is the subplot title and the other entries are frequency values (a single value or band edges). New code should use :class:`dict` or None.

tmin.description: First and last times to include, in seconds. None uses the first or last time present in the data. Default is tmin=None, tmax=None (all times).

tmax.description: First and last times to include, in seconds. None uses the first or last time present in the data. Default is tmin=None, tmax=None (all times).

proj.description: Whether to apply SSP projection vectors before spectral estimation. Default is False.

bandwidth.description: The bandwidth of the multi taper windowing function in Hz. The default value is a window half-bandwidth of 4 Hz.

adaptive.description: Use adaptive weights to combine the tapered spectra into PSD (slow, use n_jobs >> 1 to speed up computation).

low_bias.description: Only use tapers with more than 90% spectral concentration within bandwidth.

normalization.description: Normalization strategy. If "full", the PSD will be normalized by the sampling rate as well as the length of the signal (as in :ref:`Nitime <nitime:users-guide>`). Default is 'length'.

ch_type.description: The channel type to plot. For 'grad', the gradiometers are collected in pairs and the mean for each pair is plotted. If None the first available channel type from order shown above is used. Defaults to None.

normalize.description: If True, each band will be divided by the total power. Defaults to False.

agg_fun.description: The function used to aggregate over frequencies. Defaults to :func:`numpy.sum` if normalize=True, else :func:`numpy.mean`.

dB.description: Whether to plot on a decibel scale. If True, plots 10 × log₁₀(spectral_power/Hz), following the application of agg_fun. Ignored if normalize=True.

sensors.description: Whether to add markers for sensor locations. If :class:`str`, should be a valid matplotlib format string (e.g., 'r+' for red plusses, see the Notes section of :meth:`~matplotlib.axes.Axes.plot`). If True (the default), black circles will be used.

names.description: Labels for the sensors. If a :class:`list`, labels should correspond to the order of channels in data. If None (default), no channel names are plotted.

mask.description: Array indicating channel-time combinations to highlight with a distinct plotting style (useful for, e.g. marking which channels at which times a statistical test of the data reaches significance). Array elements set to True will be plotted with the parameters given in mask_params. Defaults to None, equivalent to an array of all False elements.

mask_params.description:
Additional plotting parameters for plotting significant sensors. Default (None) equals:

dict(marker='o', markerfacecolor='w', markeredgecolor='k',
        linewidth=0, markersize=4)

contours.description: The number of contour lines to draw. If 0, no contours will be drawn. If a positive integer, that number of contour levels are chosen using the matplotlib tick locator (may sometimes be inaccurate, use array for accuracy). If array-like, the array values are used as the contour levels. The values should be in µV for EEG, fT for magnetometers and fT/m for gradiometers. If colorbar=True, the colorbar will have ticks corresponding to the contour levels. Default is 6.

outlines.description: The outlines to be drawn. If 'head', the default head scheme will be drawn. If dict, each key refers to a tuple of x and y positions, the values in 'mask_pos' will serve as image mask. Alternatively, a matplotlib patch object can be passed for advanced masking options, either directly or as a function that returns patches (required for multi-axis plots). If None, nothing will be drawn. Defaults to 'head'.

image_interp.description: The image interpolation to be used. Options are 'cubic' (default) to use :class:`scipy.interpolate.CloughTocher2DInterpolator`, 'nearest' to use :class:`scipy.spatial.Voronoi` or 'linear' to use :class:`scipy.interpolate.LinearNDInterpolator`.

extrapolate.description:
Options:

  • 'box'

    Extrapolate to four points placed to form a square encompassing all data points, where each side of the square is three times the range of the data in the respective dimension.

  • 'local' (default for MEG sensors)

    Extrapolate only to nearby points (approximately to points closer than median inter-electrode distance). This will also set the mask to be polygonal based on the convex hull of the sensors.

  • 'head' (default for non-MEG sensors)

    Extrapolate out to the edges of the clipping circle. This will be on the head circle when the sensors are contained within the head circle, but it can extend beyond the head when sensors are plotted outside the head circle.

border.description: Value to extrapolate to on the topomap borders. If 'mean' (default), then each extrapolated point has the average value of its neighbours.

res.description: The resolution of the topomap image (number of pixels along each side).

size.description: Side length of each subplot in inches.

vlim.description:
Lower and upper bounds of the colormap, typically a numeric value in the same units as the data. Elements of the :class:`tuple` may also be callable functions which take in a :class:`NumPy array <numpy.ndarray>` and return a scalar.

If both entries are None, the bounds are set at ± the maximum absolute value of the data (yielding a colormap with midpoint at 0), or (0, max(abs(data))) if the (possibly baselined) data are all-positive. Providing None for just one entry will set the corresponding boundary at the min/max of the data. If vlim="joint", will compute the colormap limits jointly across all topomaps of the same channel type (instead of separately for each topomap), using the min/max of the data for that channel type. Defaults to (None, None).

colorbar.description: Plot a colorbar in the rightmost column of the figure.

cbar_fmt.description: Formatting string for colorbar tick labels. See :ref:`formatspec` for details. If 'auto', is equivalent to '%0.3f' if dB=False and '%0.1f' if dB=True. Defaults to 'auto'.

units.description: The units to use for the colorbar label. Ignored if colorbar=False. If None the label will be "AU" indicating arbitrary units. Default is None.

n_jobs.description: The number of jobs to run in parallel. If -1, it is set to the number of CPU cores. Requires the :mod:`joblib` package. None (default) is a marker for 'unset' that will be interpreted as n_jobs=1 (sequential execution) unless the call is performed under a :class:`joblib:joblib.parallel_config` context manager that sets another value for n_jobs.

verbose.description: Control verbosity of the logging output. If None, use the default verbosity level. See the :ref:`logging documentation <tut-logging>` and :func:`mne.verbose` for details. Should only be passed as a keyword argument.

plot_epochs_psd_topomap.description: Plot the topomap of the power spectral density across epochs.

sfreq.description: The sample frequency. If None, data will be displayed in samples (not seconds).

first_samp.description: The index of the first sample. Recordings made on Neuromag systems number samples relative to the system start (not relative to the beginning of the recording). In such cases the raw.first_samp attribute can be passed here. Default is 0.

color.description: Dictionary of event_id integers as keys and colors as values. If None, colors are automatically drawn from a default list (cycled through if number of events longer than list of default colors). Color can be any valid :ref:`matplotlib color <matplotlib:colors_def>`.

equal_spacing.description: Use equal spacing between events in y-axis.

on_missing.description: Can be 'raise' (default) to raise an error, 'warn' to emit a warning, or 'ignore' to ignore when event numbers from event_id are missing from :term:`events`. When numbers from :term:`events` are missing from event_id they will be ignored and a warning emitted; consider using verbose='error' in this case.

verbose.description: Control verbosity of the logging output. If None, use the default verbosity level. See the :ref:`logging documentation <tut-logging>` and :func:`mne.verbose` for details. Should only be passed as a keyword argument.

plot_events.description: Plot :term:`events` to get a visual display of the paradigm.

picks.description: Channels to include. Slices and lists of integers will be interpreted as channel indices. In lists, channel type strings (e.g., ['meg', 'eeg']) will pick channels of those types, channel name strings (e.g., ['MEG0111', 'MEG2623'] will pick the given channels. Can also be the string values 'all' to pick all channels, or 'data' to pick :term:`data channels`. None (default) will pick all channels. Bad channels are included by default. Note that channels in info['bads'] will be included if their names or indices are explicitly provided.

exclude.description: Channels names to exclude from being shown. If 'bads', the bad channels are excluded.

ylim.description: Y-axis limits for plots (after scaling has been applied). :class:`dict` keys should match channel types; valid keys are for instance eeg, mag, grad, misc, csd, .. (example: ylim=dict(eeg=[-20, 20])). If None, the y-axis limits will be set automatically by matplotlib. Defaults to None.

xlim.description: Limits for the X-axis of the plots.

proj.description: If true SSP projections are applied before display. If 'interactive', a check box for reversible selection of SSP projection vectors will be shown. If 'reconstruct', projection vectors will be applied and then M/EEG data will be reconstructed via field mapping to reduce the signal bias caused by projection.

hline.description: The values at which to show an horizontal line.

units.description: The units of the channel types used for axes labels. If None, defaults to dict(eeg='µV', grad='fT/cm', mag='fT').

scalings.description: The scalings of the channel types to be applied for plotting. If None, defaults to dict(eeg=1e6, grad=1e13, mag=1e15).

titles.description: The titles associated with the channels. If None, defaults to dict(eeg='EEG', grad='Gradiometers', mag='Magnetometers').

gfp.description:
Plot the global field power (GFP) or the root mean square (RMS) of the data. For MEG data, this will plot the RMS. For EEG, it plots GFP, i.e. the standard deviation of the signal across channels. The GFP is equivalent to the RMS of an average-referenced signal.

  • True

    Plot GFP or RMS (for EEG and MEG, respectively) and traces for all channels.

  • 'only'

    Plot GFP or RMS (for EEG and MEG, respectively), and omit the traces for individual channels.

The color of the GFP/RMS trace will be green if spatial_colors=False, and black otherwise.

window_title.description: The title to put at the top of the figure.

spatial_colors.description: If True, the lines are color coded by mapping physical sensor coordinates into color values. Spatially similar channels will have similar colors. Bad channels will be dotted. If False, the good channels are plotted black and bad channels red. If 'auto', uses True if channel locations are present, and False if channel locations are missing or if the data contains only a single channel. Defaults to 'auto'.

zorder.description: Which channels to put in the front or back. Only matters if spatial_colors is used. If str, must be std or unsorted (defaults to unsorted). If std, data with the lowest standard deviation (weakest effects) will be put in front so that they are not obscured by those with stronger effects. If unsorted, channels are z-sorted as in the evoked instance. If callable, must take one argument: a numpy array of the same dimensionality as the evoked raw data; and return a list of unique integers corresponding to the number of channels.

selectable.description: Whether to use interactive features. If True (default), it is possible to paint an area to draw topomaps. When False, the interactive features are disabled. Disabling interactive features reduces memory consumption and is useful when using axes parameter to draw multiaxes figures.

time_unit.description: The units for the time axis, can be "s" (default) or "ms".

highlight.description: Segments of the data to highlight by means of a light-yellow background color. Can be used to put visual emphasis on certain time periods. The time periods must be specified as array-like objects in the form of (t_start, t_end) in the unit given by the time_unit parameter. Multiple time periods can be specified by passing an array-like object of individual time periods (e.g., for 3 time periods, the shape of the passed object would be (3, 2). If None, no highlighting is applied.

verbose.description: Control verbosity of the logging output. If None, use the default verbosity level. See the :ref:`logging documentation <tut-logging>` and :func:`mne.verbose` for details. Should only be passed as a keyword argument.

plot_evoked.description:
Left click to a line shows the channel name. Selecting an area by clicking and holding left mouse button plots a topographic map of the painted area.

Note

If bad channels are not excluded they are shown in red.

picks.description: Channels to include. Slices and lists of integers will be interpreted as channel indices. In lists, channel type strings (e.g., ['meg', 'eeg']) will pick channels of those types, channel name strings (e.g., ['MEG0111', 'MEG2623'] will pick the given channels. Can also be the string values 'all' to pick all channels, or 'data' to pick :term:`data channels`. None (default) will pick all channels. Bad channels are included by default. Note that channels in info['bads'] will be included if their names or indices are explicitly provided. This parameter can also be used to set the order the channels are shown in, as the channel image is sorted by the order of picks.

exclude.description: Channels names to exclude from being shown. If 'bads', the bad channels are excluded.

clim.description: Color limits for plots (after scaling has been applied). e.g. clim = dict(eeg=[-20, 20]). Valid keys are eeg, mag, grad, misc. If None, the clim parameter for each channel equals the pyplot default.

proj.description: If true SSP projections are applied before display. If 'interactive', a check box for reversible selection of SSP projection vectors will be shown.

units.description: The units of the channel types used for axes labels. If None, defaults to dict(eeg='µV', grad='fT/cm', mag='fT').

scalings.description: The scalings of the channel types to be applied for plotting. If None,` defaults to dict(eeg=1e6, grad=1e13, mag=1e15).

titles.description: The titles associated with the channels. If None, defaults to dict(eeg='EEG', grad='Gradiometers', mag='Magnetometers').

colorbar.description: If True, plot a colorbar. Defaults to True.

mask.description: An array of booleans of the same shape as the data. Entries of the data that correspond to False in the mask are masked (see do_mask below). Useful for, e.g., masking for statistical significance.

mask_style.description: If mask is not None: if 'contour', a contour line is drawn around the masked areas (True in mask). If 'mask', entries not True in mask are shown transparently. If 'both', both a contour and transparency are used. If None, defaults to 'both' if mask is not None, and is ignored otherwise.

mask_alpha.description: A float between 0 and 1. If mask is not None, this sets the alpha level (degree of transparency) for the masked-out segments. I.e., if 0, masked-out segments are not visible at all. Defaults to .25.

time_unit.description: The units for the time axis, can be "ms" or "s" (default).

show_names.description: Determines if channel names should be plotted on the y axis. If False, no names are shown. If True, ticks are set automatically by matplotlib and the corresponding channel names are shown. If "all", all channel names are shown. If "auto", is set to False if picks is None, to True if picks contains 25 or more entries, or to "all" if picks contains fewer than 25 entries.

group_by.description:
If a dict, the values must be picks, and axes must also be a dict with matching keys, or None. If axes is None, one figure and one axis will be created for each entry in group_by.Then, for each entry, the picked channels will be plotted to the corresponding axis. If titles are None, keys will become plot titles. This is useful for e.g. ROIs. Each entry must contain only one channel type. For example:

group_by=dict(Left_ROI=[1, 2, 3, 4], Right_ROI=[5, 6, 7, 8])

If None, all picked channels are plotted to the same axis.

layout_scale.description: Scaling factor for adjusting the relative size of the layout on the canvas.

color.description: Everything matplotlib accepts to specify colors. If not list-like, the color specified will be repeated. If None, colors are automatically drawn.

border.description: Matplotlib borders style to be used for each sensor plot.

ylim.description: Y-axis limits for plots (after scaling has been applied). :class:`dict` keys should match channel types; valid keys are for instance eeg, mag, grad, misc, csd, .. (example: ylim=dict(eeg=[-20, 20])). If None, the y-axis limits will be set automatically by matplotlib. Defaults to None.

scalings.description: The scalings of the channel types to be applied for plotting. If None,` defaults to dict(eeg=1e6, grad=1e13, mag=1e15).

title.description: Title of the figure.

proj.description: If true SSP projections are applied before display. If 'interactive', a check box for reversible selection of SSP projection vectors will be shown.

vline.description: The values at which to show a vertical line.

fig_background.description: A background image for the figure. This must work with a call to plt.imshow. Defaults to None.

merge_grads.description: Whether to use RMS value of gradiometer pairs. Only works for Neuromag data. Defaults to False.

legend.description: If True, create a legend based on evoked.comment. If False, disable the legend. Otherwise, the legend is created and the parameter value is passed as the location parameter to the matplotlib legend call. It can be an integer (e.g. 0 corresponds to upper right corner of the plot), a string (e.g. 'upper right'), or a tuple (x, y coordinates of the lower left corner of the legend in the axes coordinate system). See matplotlib documentation for more details.

background_color.description: Background color. Typically 'k' (black) or 'w' (white; default).

exclude.description: Channels names to exclude from the plot. If 'bads', the bad channels are excluded. By default, exclude is set to 'bads'.

select.description: Whether to enable the lasso-selection tool to enable the user to select channels. The selected channels will be available in fig.lasso.selection.

plot_evoked_topo.description: Clicking on the plot of an individual sensor opens a new figure showing the evoked response for the selected sensor.

times.description: The time point(s) to plot. If "auto", the number of axes determines the amount of time point(s). If axes is also None, at most 10 topographies will be shown with a regular time spacing between the first and last time instant. If "peaks", finds time points automatically by checking for local maxima in global field power. If "interactive", the time can be set interactively at run-time by using a slider.

average.description: The time window (in seconds) around a given time point to be used for averaging. For example, 0.2 would translate into a time window that starts 0.1 s before and ends 0.1 s after the given time point. If the time window exceeds the duration of the data, it will be clipped. Different time windows (one per time point) can be provided by passing an array-like object (e.g., [0.1, 0.2, 0.3]). If None (default), no averaging will take place.

ch_type.description: The channel type to plot. For 'grad', the gradiometers are collected in pairs and the RMS for each pair is plotted. If None the first available channel type from order shown above is used. Defaults to None.

scalings.description: The scalings of the channel types to be applied for plotting. If None, defaults to dict(eeg=1e6, grad=1e13, mag=1e15).

proj.description: If true SSP projections are applied before display. If 'interactive', a check box for reversible selection of SSP projection vectors will be shown. If 'reconstruct', projection vectors will be applied and then M/EEG data will be reconstructed via field mapping to reduce the signal bias caused by projection.

sensors.description: Whether to add markers for sensor locations. If :class:`str`, should be a valid matplotlib format string (e.g., 'r+' for red plusses, see the Notes section of :meth:`~matplotlib.axes.Axes.plot`). If True (the default), black circles will be used.

show_names.description: If True, show channel names next to each sensor marker. If callable, channel names will be formatted using the callable; e.g., to delete the prefix 'MEG ' from all channel names, pass the function lambda x: x.replace('MEG ', ''). If mask is not None, only non-masked sensor names will be shown.
